title: Prevent transient recovery-lock contention from interrupting streaming during shell spawning
description: On macOS, concurrent shell process spawning can temporarily retain inherited recovery-lock descriptors after the parent closes them. RecoveryLease::acquire uses immediate File::try_lock and relies on close for release; transient contention becomes a persistence error that interrupts a healthy stream. Confirmed at 2026-10-25 18:19:48 local for session 308a34d0-20a1-4209-b979-9e6d4331faa4 in ~/.fspec/logs/private/fspec-combined.log.2026-10-25:1149. Reproduced against compiled production libraries: 39/50574 and 29/51911 failed lease acquisitions during shell spawning; no-spawn and explicit-unlock controls passed. Commit f0eb0759 did not change this lease behavior. Add acceptance criteria and regression tests for spawn overlap and short-lived contention; implement explicit lock release and bounded contention handling while preserving deletion lock order, retained originals, and independent-session progress. Historical lock-holder PID was not logged; the mechanism is independently reproduced. Detailed research and reproduction evidence are attached.
rules: [0] Recovery lease release explicitly unlocks the existing lock inode; transient contention retries for a finite deadline and persistent contention preserves WouldBlock without weakening mutual exclusion or session deletion lock order.
examples: [0] A short-lived recovery lease holder releases after 40 ms; opening the persistence spool waits within a bounded deadline and retains authentic pending output instead of interrupting the stream.

[1] While a session recovery lock remains held beyond the retry budget, another session still progresses and the waiting session returns a typed contention error without stealing or deleting the lock.
[2] Concurrent shell spawning does not prolong a released recovery lock or interrupt authentic persisted output; dropping a lease explicitly unlocks its shared file description.

scenarios.name: Short recovery contention preserves authentic pending output
Persistent contention is bounded and isolated
Shell spawning does not extend released recovery ownership
Non contention filesystem failures propagate immediately

The oversized existing streaming file will be mechanically separated into decoder and unit-test modules without changing their behavior before the ordered-map repair.
examples: [0] The provider delivers reverse-arriving fragmented ordinary calls at indexes 0 through 31, native Done at 32, and trailing work at 33. On tool_calls finish or EOF after a stop finish, all earlier side effects complete in index order, Done is genuinely accepted, and trailing work is cancelled; a nonstreaming JSON vector behaves identically.

scenarios.name: Tool finish flush preserves provider index order before Done
EOF flush preserves provider index order before Done

title: Preserve continuation budgets and goal rejection counts across recovery dispatch
description: The shared agent loop calls sync_completion_contract_for_user_turn for real inputs and synthetic outer recovery retries alike. The helper unconditionally resets continue_nudges_used and always calls set_session_goal, which resets registry rejections even for the same goal. This violates CONT-002 real-user-turn budget boundaries and CONT-003 goal-lifetime rejection counting. Separate state synchronization from genuine user-turn resets and goal-change resets. Cover automatic compaction, loop-abort corrective retries, repeated unchanged goals and genuine new tasks. Preserve CONT-008 generation/race guards and CONT-009 arming order; ordinary in-stream nudges already avoid this helper. Source-confirmed and pre-existing, not attributed solely to October changes.
rules: [0] Only an admitted genuine user input resets the per-task zero-progress nudge budget. Automatic compaction and loop-abort corrective dispatch synchronize the completion contract without starting a new task.

[1] Done rejections belong to the active goal lifetime, not a dispatch or user-turn lifetime. Resynchronizing the same goal preserves registry and inner rejection accounting; replacing or clearing the goal resets it.

[2] Recovery and genuine dispatch retain CONT-008 goal generation/replacement guards and CONT-009 arming before output/provider construction; four rejected Done calls must still reach escalation across recovery.
examples: [0] Automatic compaction after one real zero-progress nudge preserves the used nudge, so a budget of one allows no extra post-recovery nudge.
[1] A repetitive-output corrective retry after one real zero-progress nudge preserves that nudge; it cannot renew a budget of one.
[2] After a task exhausts its one-nudge budget, a genuine next user task receives exactly one fresh nudge.
[3] Two rejected Done calls before automatic compaction and two after it reach the four-rejection human-review threshold for the unchanged goal.
[4] Two rejected Done calls before a repetitive-output corrective retry and two after it reach the same four-rejection human-review threshold.
[5] A real next user message with an unchanged goal preserves earlier Done rejections, including when the user sets the same goal text and verification again.
[6] Replacing an active goal starts fresh rejection accounting for the replacement; clearing it removes the contract and resets both rejection counts without resurrecting the old goal.

scenarios.name: Automatic compaction preserves the consumed nudge budget
Loop-abort recovery preserves the consumed nudge budget
A genuine next user task receives a fresh nudge budget
Rejections across automatic compaction reach goal escalation
Rejections across loop-abort recovery reach goal escalation
Genuine user dispatch and identical goal writes preserve rejections
Replacing and clearing a goal reset its rejection accounting

title: Settle custom provider stops without dropping trailing usage or waiting for EOF
description: Rhai handle_stop marks the parser terminated, suppressing later usage-only frames, while stream_http continues polling until [DONE] or EOF. Define and test a coherent stop/usage/error lifecycle, including usage after finish_reason, stop followed by a pending connection, and stop followed by transport failure. Existing bug227 fixtures generally put usage before stop, and a post-stop transport-failure test deliberately expects failure; reconcile that contract before changing semantics. Preserve fail-closed terminal validation and accurate request settlement. Source-confirmed plumbing issue; user-installed scripts were not audited.
rules: [0] A script stop ends content, not transport parsing: later usage remains observable until [DONE] or clean EOF; post-stop text/tools cannot extend the completed content.

[1] Explicit [DONE] settles immediately without reading EOF; clean EOF after stop succeeds, missing terminal evidence and pre-boundary transport errors remain typed failures. Stop alone on an open connection is not successful settlement.
[2] The actual rig adapter settles exact physical usage before releasing buffered executable calls, so native Done cannot conceal trailing usage or failure.
examples: [0] A stop then usage then [DONE] on a connection still open produces exact final usage without waiting for EOF.
[1] A stop then usage then clean EOF preserves usage; a post-stop body failure stays an error with no successful final or executable tools.
[2] Missing terminal evidence fails; stop-only open transport remains pending and cancellation closes it.
[3] An attributed armed native Done queued before stop and trailing usage settles physical tokens once before accepting completion.

scenarios.name: Native Done cannot discard trailing physical usage
DONE settles trailing usage without waiting for EOF
Clean EOF after stop retains trailing usage

Missing terminal evidence remains a failure
Stop alone does not invent transport success

description: Discovery/design follow-up to CONT-011, PROV-148 and PROV-149. Codex protocol continuation is separate from outer /continue: it follows selected end_turn:false or interrupted responses, but replay rejects non-text output (including reasoning, hosted search, refusal sections and empty output) and caps follow-ups at three. These are explicitly specified restrictions, so do not silently label them accidental bugs or weaken safety/refusal handling. Decide which typed items are replayable, how native encrypted reasoning/history validation participates, and how protocol bounds and /continue budgets are communicated and accounted. Then specify and test complete physical follow-up requests, cancellation, admission, usage and failure behavior for the approved policy. This is not the profile-default lifecycle work already tracked by CONT-010. Research attached.
rules: [0] Only eligible current-response assistant output_text, typed reasoning summaries/encrypted content and negotiated completed hosted search may replay, preserving exact validated items and order; no unknown native fields/families or empty output.

[1] Refusal suppresses protocol replay; filtering, budget limits, failed and incomplete client-tool outcomes cannot continue. Ordinary successful client tools retain generic handoff and exact paired IDs.

[2] Retain three internal follow-ups independently of transport recovery and outer nudge/genuine-user budgets; full serialized admission and account/model/generation/ancestry checks apply to every physical request, with once-only measured billing even on failure.

[3] Publish typed checkpoint only after successful chain settlement; cancellation, reset, changed account/model/history or admission/cap failure cannot install stale output. No new durable/delta store, retry system or safety bypass.
examples: [0] A local completed or interrupted response with text, owned encrypted reasoning and negotiated hosted search sends one exact typed follow-up and settles physical usage once.
[1] Refusal with end_turn false settles visibly without another request; malformed/empty/unknown output fails and incomplete calls never execute.
[2] An endless typed chain stops after four physical responses despite a transport replacement, and admission growth/cancellation/generation/account changes prevent stale follow-ups.
[3] A real CLI tool-result and outer nudge flow preserves native call IDs, exact billing and independent protocol limits; genuine user/recovery budget controls remain unchanged.
architectureNotes: [0] Native HITL approved typed-continuation-design.md. Extend only Codex Terminal replay with a narrow validator over existing CodexItem types; retain generation/AttemptAuthority, stored account/lifecycle, full-DAG model/ancestry, native capability and physical admission gates. Refusal and unsafe/empty/unknown output never trigger follow-ups; preserve three protocol follow-ups and independent transport/outer/genuine-user budgets. Settle trustworthy physical terminal usage before replay rejection, with one final publication only on chain success; no shared Responses/Copilot defaults, durable/delta store, new retry/settings policy or arbitrary native replay. Validate actual loopback model/CLI requests plus existing account/lineage/recovery controls.

scenarios.name: Typed protocol tools and outer nudges retain separate accounting
Refusal settles visibly without protocol or outer continuation
Known typed output continues with exact owned items
Refusal and unsafe terminals never trigger protocol replay
Empty unknown and malformed continuation output fail closed
Protocol limits stay finite across transport replacement
Admission and cancellation cannot publish partial typed lineage
Generation and account changes invalidate protocol authority
Genuine follow ups preserve typed ancestry and reject rewrites

title: Allow repeated Gemini tool invocations without duplicate journal admission failures
description: P1 review finding in commit 144653b0: Gemini uses function names as tool IDs, but StreamJournal keeps requested, started, and result identities keyed by that ID across the turn. Calling the same tool twice can fail journal admission or dispatch and interrupt a valid agent turn. See the attached review finding for evidence, reproduction, and regression-test guidance.
rules: [0] Each Gemini function invocation has a distinct internal identity across response attempts; provider function names and thought signatures remain unchanged, duplicate dispatch is refused, and cold replay never reexecutes tools.
examples: [0] Given a Gemini provider that requests the same reading tool twice with different paths and signed calls, When a real background streaming turn consumes both requests and a subsequent response attempt repeats that tool, Then each invocation executes once with a distinct durable identity and authentic result while physical continuations preserve function names and signatures

[1] Given an acknowledged Gemini tool invocation, When its internal identity is dispatched twice and the process restores before capturing the genuine result, Then duplicate dispatch is refused and repeated cold replay retains outcome-unknown without repeating the side effect or merging another invocation result

Duplicate dispatch and cold recovery never repeat a side effect

title: Avoid full transcript replay on every streamed journal append
description: P1 review finding in commit 144653b0: JournalStore::append enumerates, reads, deserializes, and projects the complete accumulated session journal for every text or thinking delta. The synchronous append runs while the process-global recovery-owner mutex is held, creating quadratic ingestion work and cross-session persistence stalls as sessions grow. See the attachment for evidence and scaling-validation guidance.
rules: [0] After validated opening, fixed-size streamed deltas use incremental sequence, identity and lifecycle indexes instead of rereading or reprojecting accumulated immutable history; cold opens and explicit reads still validate corruption and completeness.

[1] Recovery ownership is serialized per session, never by a process-global mutex held across filesystem work. Admission remains durable before publication, idempotent on retry, and rejects deleted owners.
examples: [0] Growing batches beyond 128 deltas after completed turns and a large authentic tool result perform bounded record reads and one lifecycle admission per new delta; a cold reopen reconstructs exact history and detects corruption or missing ordinals.
[1] While session A is blocked at a real filesystem publication boundary, session B durably admits and publishes its own event; retrying A preserves identity and deletion still retires its lane.

scenarios.name: Long streaming sessions require bounded admission work
Cold opening validates immutable history before admission
An unrelated session progresses during a stalled journal append
Retried publication retains durable identity

title: Recover TUI transcript hydration after a server generation change
description: P2 review finding in commit 144653b0: transcript page failures retain the assembler cursor and pinned snapshot, while /resume does not reset generation-bound state once a cursor exists. A missed session-clear event or concurrent archive installation can leave the tab polling an obsolete generation indefinitely, hiding subsequent content until the tab is reopened. See the attachment for reproduction and safe recovery requirements.
rules: [0] Known generation mismatch atomically invalidates cursor, partial bytes, pinned snapshot and inflight identity; /resume can hydrate the new generation without reopening. Replace old generation rendering, never append a second full snapshot.

[1] Transport failures remain distinguishable and retain displayed content and deduplication. Late responses from an invalidated hydration attempt must not mutate current rendering, including an archive-install race.
examples: [0] An open tab misses clear, then /resume displays new-generation content once in order and no old-generation text, without closing the tab.

[1] Archive installation changes generation after a partial page; recovery discards the old bytes and late page, then renders the authoritative transcript once. A normal reconnect retains existing content once.

scenarios.name: Resume recovers a missed server clear without reopening
Archive installation during partial hydration recovers atomically
Unchanged generation reconnect preserves deduplication
Transient page failures preserve displayed history

title: Journal terminal outcomes emitted by the outer agent error fallback
description: Retain exactly one safe durable failure per abandoned outer agent request, preserving actionable live diagnostics and model-history separation. Human approval 2026-10-25 supersedes the earlier hold conditional on native ACDD card/status/Markdown updates (completed before production edits). Approved bounded extraction keeps all touched Rust files below 300 lines, preserving locks, cancellation epochs/notify, handler/drop order, counters and Idle-before-Done. Seven real-path scenarios cover invalid preparation, failed/exhausted overflow recovery, applied-compaction budget exhaustion, inner-error deduplication, successful recovery and failed explicit-builder retry. Mechanical extraction preserved 4 behavioral reds/2 greens and all 5 unchanged MCP source contracts before repair. Final settlement calls finish_outer_failure on the original output; owned recovery borrows that same output instead of allocating another journal. Preserve immutable CompactionFailed while admitting one actionable live Error without another terminal. All seven acceptance cases green; broader validation caveats are explicit in acdd-validation.md. No global publication hook, synthetic identity, terminal rewrite, model-original prose, gate bypass, unrelated card/test/source-shape fix, commit or push.
rules: [0] Only an abandoned final outer fallback receives a safe durable terminal failure on the original request owner before publication; inner-stream terminal errors deduplicate and successful automatic recovery gains no spurious failure. Terminal prose never enters model originals.

[1] When successful in-turn compaction exhausts the automatic continuation budget, the final request must retain one safe failure rather than a prematurely finalized success. Preserve request identity, exactly-once terminals and Idle-before-Done; do not alter immutable completed journal records.

[2] If a failed explicit builder retry already has a durable CompactionFailed terminal, retain that immutable outcome and publish its actionable outer Error diagnostic once without appending another terminal or polluting model originals. Existing provider-error deduplication remains unchanged.
examples: [0] Invalid request preparation and failed/exhausted outer overflow recovery survive repeated cold replay as one safe ordered terminal outcome. An already-journaled inner error remains single; successful recovery has no final failure.

[1] Four consecutive successful inference turns each apply compaction: three continue automatically, the fourth exhausts the budget. No fifth inference starts; the fourth request has exactly one durable safe provider failure on repeated cold replay, not an inner completed terminal.

[2] A user retries a failed compaction builder and it fails again with retry-later guidance. The live Error still contains that guidance, the session returns Idle, no ordinary inference restarts, and repeated cold replay retains exactly one safe failure per abandoned request.
architectureNotes: [0] Human approval 2026-10-25: "well you have to do it acdd via fspec.. either update the existing card and set the right work status, and attach new markdown documentation to that card then start it". Supersedes prior extraction-review-plan approval hold only for the concrete dependency-preserving bounded extraction and minimal outer terminal fix. Baseline testing has 3 behavioral reds, 2 passing controls; add applied-compaction budget control before implementing. Preserve prior uncommitted BUG253/256/257 work and BUG254/255 holds.

[1] Validation refinement within BUG258 terminal routing: existing explicit-builder retry journals CompactionFailed as a warning; the outer Error was previously a separate live diagnostic. Canonical fallback admission now suppresses that diagnostic, failing the unchanged repeated-builder-failure regression. Add a real-path acceptance test first, then a bounded StreamJournal admission distinction: allow one live ProviderError diagnostic after acknowledged CompactionFailed without appending/replacing a terminal. Keep provider-error dedup, immutable outcomes, same request identity and existing emit path; no global publication hook or runtime redesign.

[2] Strengthened seventh-case safe-failure counting exposed an existing second BackgroundOutput allocation inside try_terminal_overflow_recovery_owned. Pass the original turn output into this owned helper (public locking wrapper may retain its independent owner) so recovery CompactionFailed and outer Error share one request/journal. This implements the approved same-owner invariant rather than concealing duplicates via another identity. Retain one immutable safe outcome, one actionable diagnostic and Idle-before-Done.
